q-2525.name: Question 1
q-2525.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={x}^{3}+{e}^{x}$ and the point $P(0,1)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(1,0).$
q-2525.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(0,1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(0) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(0,1)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(1,0)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(1))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(0)} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

2e3

EXPLANATION

We start by calculating the derivative of f at the point (0,1).

f(x)=x3+exf′(x)=3x2+exf′(0)=1

Since (0,1) lies on y=f(x), we know that the corresponding point (1,0) lies on y=f−1(x).

q-76128.name: Question 2
q-76128.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=1+2{e}^{x+1}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3).$
q-76128.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(3).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(3)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(3) & =x \\ f(x) & =3 \\ 1+2{e}^{x+1} & =3 \\ 2{e}^{x+1} & =2 \\ {e}^{x+1} & =1 \\ x+1 & =0 \\ x & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(3)=-1.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(-1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =1+2{e}^{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{x+1} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2{e}^{0} \\ {f}^{′}(-1) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The following table gives the values of f(x),f′(x),g(x), and g′(x) at some points. Find (g⋅f−1)′(3) of the product of functions.

x f(x) f′(x) g(x) g′(x)
3 5 −2 −3 1
−2 3 −4 −2 −5
a
−25
b
−14
c
−54
d
45
e
54
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the derivative of the inverse f−1(x) is (f−1)′(x)=1f′(f−1(x)).

Using this, and the product rule, the derivative of the function g(x)f−1(x) is (g⋅f−1)′(x)=g′(x)f−1(x)+g(x)f′(f−1(x)).

Substituting x=3, we have (g⋅f−1)′(3)=g′(3)f−1(3)+g(3)f′(f−1(3)).

From the table, we obtain f−1(3)=−2, g(3)=−3, g′(3)=1, and f′(−2)=−4. Therefore,

(g⋅f−1)′(3)=g′(3)f−1(3)+g(3)f′(f−1(3))=1⋅(−2)+−3f′(−2)=−2+(−3)(−4)=−54.
